newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria May unemployment falls to 14.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria May unemployment falls to 14.8 pct.

text.p: The number of unemployed people in Bulgaria fell to 567,320 or 14.8 percent of the workforce in May from 584,851 in April, a National Labour Exchange (NLE) official said on Thursday.
"Unemployment dipped despite ongoing closures of state firms and lay-offs in the public sector as new seasonal jobs in tourism and farming were offered last month," the official told Reuters.
However, an underlying upward trend for the unemployment rate was in place as Bulgaria moved along the path of structural reform agreed with international lenders, the official said.
Crisis-ridden Bulgaria has pledged to close down state loss-making firms and reduce red tape under a $657 million reform and funding agreement with the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
Under preliminary NLE estimates some 160,000 employees in the public sector and industrial plants were expected to be laid off this year as a result of structural reform.

The World Bank has approved a $25 million loan for severance payments and compensation for professional retraining, and a further $80 million has been earmarked for lending in the course of the reform.

Bulgaria's average unemployment rate for 1996 was 11.1 percent, down 0.3 points from 1995. Unemployment peaked in January 1994, when 16.6 percent of the workforce was jobless. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 911 88
